newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Supported by fresh bunker demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Supported by fresh bunker demand.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market was quiet on Monday but prices were well supported following gains in the swaps market, which were strengthened by fresh demand from the bunker market, traders said.
"The market seemed to be quite well supported by demand from the bunker market today," the trader said, expecting an uptrend after recent sluggish trade.
Suppliers were waiting for price gains and stayed on the sidelines, traders said.
On Monday, the 380-cst grade fuel oil traded at $92.50 per tonne for May 2-6 lifting.
Fuel oil swaps edged up on expectations of fresh demand from the local bunker market as supplies in South Korea tighten, traders said.
On late Tuesday, April swaps rose to $98.75/$99.25 from Monday's $98.00/$99.00. May advanced to $97.75/$98.25 from $97.00/$97.50.
Traders said South Korea, Singapore's main competitor, has no more fuel oil for April and has raised bunker prices by $2.00 per tonne, decreasing its price competitiveness.
Bunker sellers in Singapore, noting improving bunker enquiries, said they were tight on supplies.
A major said he was still seeking to buy the 380-cst grade for May lifting.
But others said supplies are not that tight as Caltex Singapore has offered to sell by tender a total of 50,000 tonnes of 380-cst and 10,000 tonnes 180-cst fuel oil.
In the first tender, Caltex offers 20,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil for April 26-28 lifting free-on-board Singapore basis, the sources said.
The second tender offers 30,000 tonnes of 380-cst and 10,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil for in-tank-transfer (ITT) on April 15.
Both tenders close on April 9 and are valid until April 10.
The LSWR market remained bearish on ample supplies, with offers down to $15.50 from Monday's $16.25, but there were no buyers.
Traders said poor demand from China and Japan would continue adding pressure to prices, traders said.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
